name: Women's USAF-style mess dress (blank: no grade or medals; CAP seal on the right side)
size_basis: Silhouette traced from images/base/mess_dress_female.webp (581x719 px) at 0.0474 in/px (same canvas and scale assumption as the Class A coat; 32.71 in tall). No real garment was measured.
landmarks_note: rects are {x,y,w,h}; polygons are [[x,y]...]; all in user units (0.01 in), origin top-left of the artwork box

tie_tab.basis: the house women's tie tab (accessories/tie-tab-inverted-v: 2.7 x 1.6 in, 0.7 in legs), centred, its top edge under the blouse collar leaves; the regulation (CAPR 39-1 4.1.2.2.1) gives the colour, the inverted V and the self-fastening tails but no dimension; the earlier traced tab was 4.27 x 4.5 in and off-centre
tie_tab.draw_order: tab first, the blouse collar leaves over it (as the blazer and the semi-formal, 4d6678dd)

front_hems.panels_note: the traced front hems of the two jacket fronts in artwork-box inches (x from the box left, y down from the box top); the figure below them, and between the fronts under the cummerbund, is the skirt (garment-mess-dress-skirt-female-*), registered to this sheet
front_hems.gap_citation: CAPR 39-1 4.1.2.1: the front opening leaves a gap of 2 to 3 in at the bottom
front_hems.cummerbund_citation: CAPR 39-1 4.1.2.2.4: the cummerbund is worn halfway between the blouse and the skirt, so the skirt starts at its lower edge
front_hems.back_note: the back extends only 2 1/2 to 3 in below the natural waist (4.1.2.1), so it is hidden behind the fronts and not drawn

sleeve_widening.chevron_fit_note: worst clearance over every ink row of the six white chevrons (4 in; 3p5 = the 3 1/2 in option at 7/8 scale), chevron visual centre on chevron_halfway, turned by the line shoulder_seam to elbow; positive = on the sleeve

documented: women's mess dress jacket and skirt with satin shawl collar (CAPR 39-1 4.1.2)
CAP seal worn over the middle button on the right side of the jacket (as on the men's, 4.1.1.1.2.3)
sleeve braid 1/2 in (1 1/2 in for general officers), 3 in from the sleeve end: separate overlay asset

the jacket ends at the traced front hems; the front opening leaves a gap of 2 to 3 in at the bottom and the back extends only 2 1/2 to 3 in below the natural waist, so below the hems and between the fronts under the cummerbund the figure is the skirt, which starts at the cummerbund's lower edge (4.1.2.1, 4.1.2.2.4, 4.1.2.3)
assumed: seal drawn at the 2 1/2 in diameter dimensioned in CAPR 39-1 Fig A6-4 (blue-background version); eagle/shield is the measured CAP Crest redraw, ring lettering set in Arial Bold outlines
shawl collar, shirt, cummerbund and cut-away geometry read off the base image
satin sheen colours sampled from the base image
tie tab size (the regulation gives none): the house 2.7 x 1.6 in tab, tails not drawn

sleeve width: the traced hanging sleeve is widened outward by up to 0.35 in between the shoulder end and the elbow (one warp of the part between the armhole seam and the outer edge) so the true-size white chevron lies on it; the regulation gives no sleeve width (ESTIMATE)
